title: Hytale Adaptive Surface: persistent geometry with selected-block materials
summary: A single creative block stores smoothing geometry and a copied material in native BlockType states. Its broad texture catalogue stays outside active asset paths; a per-world pack activates only saved-world materials before clients join. Placement selects the clicked block from Hytale interaction data.
problem_class: adaptive block geometry and selective material texture loading
problem_description: One smoothing block must form slopes/corners, retain its shape/material across world saves, and copy the exact block a player right-clicked without rebuilding a large client atlas during play or preventing world startup.
context: Zytale Adaptive Surface 0.9.3 on Hytale 0.6.8. The sole inventory item is Adaptive Surface (Blocks → Soils). Java plugin and generated asset pack run in tandem. Earlier broad HD asset loading caused client texture failures; the later world ZIP was initially disabled by save config. Legacy atlas resizing also produced diagonal alpha artifacts. The final click-selection implementation was positively reported by the user but not instrumented with client click traces.
inputs: native cube textures and material variants
constraints: client assets must be registered before join
no runtime asset registrations during placement
one visible creative item and no command
new learned textures become available after restart
known_attempts: full HD catalogue active at startup
placement interaction sync data for clicked material

solution_versions.description: Use native BlockType.State.Definitions to persist each material/geometry combination behind one Adaptive Surface item; generate Blockbench-compatible masked-quad models and collision boxes.
changes: Assign stable state IDs for material, orientation and topology
Keep the source item linked to every state
Refresh local topology after placement or break events
advantages: Persistent shapes without separate block entities
disadvantages: Original material and UV atlas strategy required further work
test_results: Earlier server fixture loaded 448 legacy states
Saved states were checked across restart

solution_versions.description: 0.8.0 activated the complete baked native-density material catalogue at startup, with 256x256 shared atlases and 32 source texels per block.
changes: Prebake 2,744 source IDs to 614 appearances and 695 variant PNGs
disadvantages: Client log recorded 3,176 failed block textures, including Unknown.png; world did not open
The exact engine atlas limit was not established

solution_versions.description: 0.9.3 keeps the full baked catalogue dormant in the JAR and builds a small active pack from each saved world. It enables the pack in save config, keeps fallback UVs native, and selects the clicked material from placement interaction data.
changes: Scan saved chunk palettes and write ZAS_ActivePack.zip before world startup
Move 0.9.1 fallback states onto native atlas and model geometry
Use matching interaction destination plus clicked target or block face to select the material
Retain material while local topology changes shape
Use current-view raycast only when no client interaction context exists
advantages: World loads with 56 active appearances in observed save
No texture rebuild or asset registration on placement
Existing saved block IDs remain valid
Unknown materials can be prepared for a future restart
disadvantages: A material first encountered during play may use stone until a later restart
Budget of 10 million HD pixels per world is a project guard, not a proven engine limit
Final click behavior lacks automated client trace
Full dedicated-server test was limited by native QUIC and shutdown errors
test_results: 0.9.1 pack load: 921 aliases, 56 appearances, zero runtime registrations
0.9.3 Gradle offline build passed with 12,124 assertions
Asset validation passed 34,300 geometry samples, 498 face mappings per atlas, 12,114 states and one creative item

metrics.reliability: User feedback positive; final click path not instrumented in client
metrics.performance: 4,784,128 active HD pixels for observed save; 56 appearances and 73 PNGs

transferability: Transfer static-versus-active asset separation, validation of save-level pack enablement, and event-target versus clicked-target distinction only after checking the target engine API. Hytale-specific model/state IDs remain project knowledge.

metrics.reliability: World joined with selective pack; final click behavior reported near-perfect by user, without automated client trace
metrics.performance: 56 active appearances and 4,784,128 HD pixels in tested save versus 614 appearances and 45,547,520 pixels in full catalogue
